rows.en:
My name is Shoji Arai, from Class 2-B.
Well then, I'll tell the first story.
Um... this is a bit sudden, but do you know what an earthbound spirit is?
When a restless spirit can't pass on and settles in one place for good, we call it an earthbound spirit.
For example, you often hear about cursed houses, don't you?
The people living there have no idea why, yet they're tormented by a spirit.
They hear moaning in the middle of the night, or footsteps and noises from rooms where no one should be.
Before long, someone in the family falls ill, or meets with some sudden misfortune...
Sometimes they even end up dead.
Then, once they move out, everything that was happening stops, as if it had all been a lie.
Quite often, that's the work of an earthbound spirit attached to the house.
The spirit is attached to the place, so it isn't a problem with the people who came to live there.
And once those people are gone, it just waits, perfectly still, for the next ones to come.
They say people who died holding a deep grudge often become earthbound spirits.
Though apparently it isn't only people; sometimes animals or the forces of nature are at work too.
The best way to get rid of an earthbound spirit is an exorcism, but some are so powerful that no exorcism can do anything about them.
With places like that, all you can do is leave them alone.
After all, no one can lay a finger on them.{p}

There are quite a lot of places like that in Japan, even today.
So, did you know our school has a place like that too?
For some reason, people who go there tend to fall down.
And when they do, they break bones, or swell up terribly.
They only fell over, yet they badly injure their arms or legs.
They didn't twist anything, and there's no dip or bump in the ground there.
And yet accidents like that never stopped.
A place like that must have an earthbound spirit, I'd say...
That's what I think, anyway.
Mind you, when I say those accidents happened, I'm talking about more than twenty years ago.
Nothing like that happens now.
No, just because it doesn't happen doesn't mean the earthbound spirit is gone.
It's still right there, even now.
But the accidents stopped.{p}Why do you think that is?
They held an exorcism
They built something to keep people out
It's a fickle spirit, so it's asleep now

Well, well, you have good instincts.
That's right.
They made it so no one could go in there.{p}So what do you think they built there?
The gym
The incinerator
A flower bed
A bronze statue

Did you know this story?
There's a flower bed behind the gym, isn't there?
That was actually the place.
A teacher back then turned it into a flower bed because so many accidents kept happening there.
Making it a flower bed didn't mean nobody went in anymore.
The gardening club members who tended it were in and out all the time, after all.
Even so, for some reason, the accidents stopped after that.
Well, compared to before, far fewer people went in and out.
Whether that was why, or whether making the flower bed did the trick, nobody can say for sure.
Still, it's a fact that nothing happened anymore.
But when the flower bed was first made, everyone was careful.
Back then, everyone knew about those accidents.
Apparently even the gardening club members were fearful when they tended the flower bed at first.
But after one year, two years, five years, ten years, nobody worried about it anymore.
They forgot.
There hadn't been a single accident since then.
Even so, since it's a big flower bed, nobody tries to step into it unless they have a very good reason.
Luckily, no delinquent ever turned up wanting to trample the flower bed, either.
Even if an accident happened now, no one but the teachers who've been here a long time would think it was because of that cursed place.{p}

But I believe an earthbound spirit is still lurking there.
Sure, people may no longer get their feet swept out from under them, but something like that happened there, after all.
That "something" is what I'm about to tell you now.
Oh, everyone.
Are you wondering how I know the story of the flower bed when nobody knows it anymore?
It's only natural to wonder.
Even now, only a very few people know it.
I didn't experience it myself, but I'm not lying.
This really happened.
It's a true story.
If you doubt me, go take a look at the flower bed later.
Of course, I can't take any responsibility for what happens.
As for who told me this story... well, does it matter?
There's no need to make an issue of that right now.
It was six years ago.{p}

Back then, the gardening club had a girl named Momoko Hayasaka, who loved flowers very much.
Hayasaka was a quiet person, and not exactly the cheerful type. But when she smiled, her dimples were just adorable, and she was honest and kind-hearted.
Every day after school, she tended the flower bed.
As if the flowers were her own flesh-and-blood brothers and sisters.
She cared for them devotedly, tenderly.
More than anyone else in the gardening club.
Flowers are living things, after all.
Perhaps the flowers could feel how Hayasaka felt, because they answered her love with magnificent blooms.
Even ordinary students with no interest in flowers would all stop when they passed the flower bed and gaze at its beauty.
Even the teachers sighed in admiration at how splendid the flower bed had become since Hayasaka started looking after it.
The season turned to June.
It was the time when purple hydrangeas, wet with rain, filled that flower bed with beautiful blossoms.{p}

The rainy season that year was especially bad; you couldn't see the sun for a single day.
It rained almost every day, and the days dragged on so gloomily that even everyone's spirits sank.
Apparently too much rain is bad for flowers, too.
Without sunlight, with rain day after day, even plants that should grow just can't.
So Hayasaka was kept busy tending the flowers every single day, even in the rain.
Of course, she didn't find it hard at all.
She was happy just to be able to care for the flowers, and she looked after them diligently every day.
But that's what did her in.
She'd never been very strong.{p}

One day, when the rainy season was almost over, she came down with pneumonia and was confined to bed. Even in bed, all she worried about was the flower bed.
Not being able to go to school was painful, agonizing, and day after day she fretted over whether the flowers were growing safely.
The pneumonia she'd caught was very serious.
Even after a week, her fever didn't break, and her condition only got worse.{p}What do you think happened to the flowers then?
The flowers grew safely
The flowers began to wither

That's right.
Even though the other gardening club members looked after them as hard as they could, the flowers gradually began to wither.
As hard as they tried, I suppose they were still no match for Hayasaka.
The flower bed that had been so beautiful and bright became a shadow of itself in no time.
Amazingly, even the hydrangeas, which can stand up to the rain, withered for some reason.
Everyone started saying the flowers were withering because they missed Hayasaka. Even so, she didn't get better.{p}

When the club members she was close to went to visit her,
"Is everyone doing well?
Nobody's wilting?"
That's what she asked.
She worried more about the flowers than about her own body, and whatever they talked about, it always ended up being the school flower bed.
The club members looked at each other and fell silent.
The truth was hard to say, but was it all right to lie to her, either...?{p}What do you think they said?
They lied and said the flowers were fine
They told her the truth: the flowers had withered

"The flowers have withered.
If you don't get better soon and look after them, Hayasaka, they'll stay droopy and we won't know what to do.
It seems we're no good at it."
They said it while doing their best to act cheerful.
They didn't say it to trouble Hayasaka.
They said it to cheer her up.
But it backfired.
She was terribly disheartened, and after that, whether they joked or talked about school, she only nodded along now and then, her mind elsewhere the whole time.
After they left, she thought about nothing but the flower bed.
If she went, the flowers would recover.
The flowers would surely recover for her.
Believing that, she left the house.{p}

And she headed for school.
Even though she could barely get out of bed.
Outside, a soft rain was falling.
The heavy, overcast sky was dark and bleak, and even though it was June, it was as cold as midwinter.
At school, the flowers were waiting for her.{p}

The next day, everyone learned of Hayasaka's death.
They say she passed away at home with a gentle smile on her face.
The gardening club members were stunned by her death.
They even wondered whether she had died of the shock because they'd visited her and said what they did.
And partly to honor her memory, they went to the flower bed.
There, they couldn't believe their eyes.{p}

The flower bed was bursting with blossoms.
And all of them hydrangeas, covering every inch.
What's more, they were bright red hydrangeas.
The hydrangeas that had been purple until yesterday had turned red, like blood.
Everyone was astonished and ran to the flower bed.
There, in the flower bed, they found Hayasaka's handkerchief.
Only then did they realize Hayasaka had come to tend the flower bed the day before.

"...Hayasaka coughed up blood."
One of them murmured in a trembling voice.
And when they looked where he was pointing, the soil had turned a dark, murky black.
Mixed in with the rain-soaked soil was an even deeper black, caked hard like the stain left after coughing up a great deal of blood.
And when they looked closely, the soil around the base of every red hydrangea stem had turned that same murky black.
More than frightened, everyone was unbearably sad.
It was from then on.
That the hydrangeas blooming in our school's flower bed turned bright red.
You've all seen them, haven't you?
Those blood-red hydrangeas.
That's the story behind them.{p}

How do I know that story, you ask?
The gardening club member who told Hayasaka the flowers had withered was actually my older brother.
I heard this story from him.
Apparently he was in love with Hayasaka.
So he thought she had died because of what he'd said, and for a long while after that, he was terribly depressed.
And even now, every year on the anniversary of her death, he goes to lay red hydrangeas on her grave.
He says those hydrangeas are her color, so they belong with her.
Maybe he's right.
I went along with him once.{p}

Of course, nothing bad happens at that flower bed now.
But I believe there's definitely an earthbound spirit there.
They say spirits latch on to you when you're kind to them.
Show them pity, and they can end up bringing disaster down on you instead.
Don't you think the spirit there might have mistaken Hayasaka's kindness to the flowers for kindness to itself?
And can't you imagine that, overjoyed, it dragged her into the spirit world?{p}

My brother said it was strange.
That Hayasaka, as gravely ill as she was, ever managed to make it to the flower bed.
Her love of flowers was almost unnatural, so maybe that got her as far as the flower bed somehow, but there was no way she'd have had the strength to get back home from there.
Didn't she breathe her last right there at the flower bed?
Didn't she die in the flower bed where she'd coughed up blood, surrounded by flowers?
And then some spiritual power must have been at work, carrying her soulless body back home, mustn't it?
He can't help thinking so.
That's the one thing he still finds strange, he says.{p}

Maybe so.
Fortunately, nothing has happened at the flower bed since then, and the gardening club members, who like flowers well enough, seem to take reasonably good care of it.
But I truly believe it.
That there's an earthbound spirit in that flower bed.
And at the same time, I'm afraid.
That someday, someone will wander in there just to make mischief.
And kick to pieces the flowers Hayasaka raised so lovingly.
When that day comes, will they get off with just a fall and a broken leg?
After all, I'd hate to think Hayasaka's soul has joined the earthbound spirit living in that flower bed.
I just hope nothing like that ever happens...
Now then, who'll be telling the next story?{p}

Yes, they held an exorcism.
But educators have their pride as so-called intellectuals to keep up, so they couldn't do it openly, and it was decided they'd do it over summer vacation.
Well, that was just the official reason; apparently the real idea was to hide it from the public eye as much as possible.{p}Who do you think they asked to perform the exorcism?
A Shinto priest
A Buddhist monk
A Catholic priest

Yes, they called in a Shinto priest, under the pretext of a groundbreaking ceremony for a small prefab storehouse.
People who didn't know seemed to think it was an awful lot of fuss, but nearly all the senior teachers gathered for it.
And they built the prefab storehouse, just as the pretext said.
Since no accidents happened while the prefab storehouse was being built, the teachers thought that was the end of it.{p}
And for a while after that nothing happened, but then one trivial incident brought the earthbound spirit back out.{p}

It was when everyone had nearly forgotten there had ever been an earthbound spirit.
The teachers must have felt safe, because they told two boys to put some desks and chairs nobody needed anymore away in that storehouse.
One carried a desk, the other a chair, and they headed for the storehouse, fooling around.
"Ando, whoever loses at rock-paper-scissors gets the desk."
"You're on, Koyama."
That's how the incident began.
And at the time, no one imagined something so horrible would happen.
They headed for the storehouse, making a racket.{p}

And so the two of them went into the storehouse.
"Hey, let's get out of here, quick."
Ando was suddenly seized by an intense terror.
Koyama was scared too, but maybe he was embarrassed to feel that way, because he started making even more noise than before.
He knocked over the desks and chairs stored there and banged on them.{p}

And that's when it happened.
With a violent bang, the open door slammed shut.{p}

The two of them remembered the feelings they'd been covering up.
Then they rushed to the door and tried to open it.
But the door wouldn't open.
As if to blow away their fear, they shouted for help from inside at the top of their lungs.
They called for help for a while, but no one came.
This prefab storehouse stood behind the school building, so people rarely passed by.
What's more, it was already past the time everyone went home.{p}

More than three hours had passed since they were shut in.
It had grown quite dark around them.
Once night fell, their families would surely come looking for them.
That alone kept them going.
Ando spoke up, sounding miserable.{p}

"But a teacher should have noticed by now.
I think they forgot about us."
Koyama was crouched on the floor, not saying a word.
Out of sheer terror, Ando yelled at Koyama.
He shoved him as he sat there with his head hanging.{p}
Then Koyama came toward him, his head still bowed.{p}

"Waaagh!"
Ando screamed in shock.
The face Koyama raised was like a monster's.
All Ando could think of now was getting out of this storehouse.
And he threw himself against the door.
"Somebody! Somebody!"
Koyama closed in on Ando as he slammed himself against the door.

"Just kidding! Scared you, didn't I, Ando?"
It was Koyama's usual voice.
"Don't scare me like that, Koyama...
I can't handle that kind of thing."
Ando's voice was still shaking.
Then he swallowed and finally caught his breath.
"Where'd you find that mask?"
"Huh? Mask...?"
"Give it a rest already."
With that, Ando tried to tear off Koyama's mask.
"Huh...?"
He backed away.
The mask was warm, and it felt just like touching human skin.{p}

"It's not a mask..."
Ando screamed.
Once the terror he had sealed away came back, he couldn't hold it down anymore.
And he beat on the door with a chair that was nearby.

"Gyaaah!"
Again and again, he hit him.
And only when Koyama fell to the floor and stopped moving did he finally stop.
Ando sank down onto the floor.{p}

The next morning, the two of them were found.
Koyama lay on the floor covered in blood, and Ando had lost his mind.
When the teachers came to the storehouse, they say the door opened easily.
This is what Ando said at the hospital, but there's no knowing what really happened.
Maybe the spirit showed him an illusion, or turned Koyama into a monster, or maybe Ando simply lost his mind out of fear.

But here's what I think.
Even shut in a storehouse, could an ordinary high school student really lose his mind so easily that he'd kill someone?
I don't know in what form, but I believe it's a fact that the earthbound spirit had some kind of effect on Ando's mind.
The proof is that the teachers acted unnaturally afterward.
When the police questioned them, about Ando, who had been a perfectly ordinary student,
'He often behaved strangely in his daily life,'
is apparently what they said.
And apparently Ando's guidance records and such were secretly rewritten.
It's a fact that the school is hiding something.
It's too late to regret enrolling at this school now, {f:you know|you know}, {a}.
This is only the beginning, after all.
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}

Maybe that's how it is.
The teachers back then turned a blind eye, even though accidents kept happening.
Maybe because there weren't any major accidents.
Well, of course, I think part of it was that the students were careful, too, and knew it was better not to go near there.
Eventually, for some reason, the accidents in that spot stopped happening.
No, maybe the accidents didn't stop; maybe we just don't know about them...
And the students and teachers who knew about it left, through graduation or transfers, and the earthbound spirit seems to have been forgotten.
But if we suppose it's sleeping now, then someday it's bound to wake up.
No, maybe it was released from its sleep long ago without our ever noticing.
I've been overhearing things lately, you see.
Oh, you mean where the place is?
These days... look, you can see it from that window.{p}Can you tell which it is?

That's right, the gym.
On that spot, they built a magnificent gym, said to be the finest of any school around here.
The construction company had a huge number of workers, and the site was full of life, apparently.
People from the neighborhood came to watch every day.
But think about it.
A gym is a place where the whole student body sometimes gathers, and they went and built one there, of all places... It makes you a little suspicious, doesn't it?
Here's what the school nurse was saying.
Huh? Oh, I'm on the health committee, you see.{p}

"I noticed when I was sorting through the injury log the other day...
At the start of August, there's always some student who gets hurt.
And every one of them is a broken bone.
That's odd for a coincidence."
And there's this story, too...{p}

Back then, this school was a baseball powerhouse and a regular at Koshien, but the principal apparently wanted indoor sports to thrive too, and that's what led to the decision to build the gym.
Simple-minded, isn't it?
You know how it is too: the popular clubs fill up fast at any school, and the students who can't win a starting spot have to scrape by as benchwarmers.
Yes, and at the worst places, you can't even make the bench; you're just a club member who runs errands.
Shigeru Asada, a third-year in the baseball club back then, was one of those.
He was quiet and kept a low profile, but his passion for baseball was second to none.
But he never landed a starting spot, never even made the bench, and was stuck chasing balls along with the juniors.
Students who can't make the team often quit, but he stayed on as a dedicated member of the baseball club.
"The next game is the last one of my high school life, so at least I want to give it my all cheering."
That's what he said; apparently he was really looking forward to it, even though he'd never get to stand on the mound.
One day, while he was picking up balls with the juniors as usual, the pitcher threw a wild pitch, and the ball went into the gym under construction.
Normally, you'd tell a junior to go fetch it, right?
But he was so good-natured that he said,
"It's okay, I'll go get it,"
and ducked under the no-entry rope and went inside.{p}

Once inside, he saw that the gym looked almost finished.
It was already evening, so the construction workers were gone, and the place was dead silent.
The crack of bats hitting balls echoed oddly well off the domed ceiling of interlocking steel beams.
Listening to that sound, he started to feel strange, somehow wistful.
Everything since he'd joined the baseball club...
"I never made the team, but it's been a fun three years...
I got to play the baseball I love, so I was happy...
Whoa, this is no time to be thinking about that.
I have to find the ball and get back."
He searched every corner of the dim gym.
"It's not anywhere..."{p}
Glancing to the side, he saw a small concrete mixer sitting there.
Look inside
Search somewhere else

"There's no way the ball got in there...
Oh, there it is!"{p}

He could see the ball in a corner of the gym.
He ran.
Between him and the ball, construction tools and who knows what were still strewn about.
Nimbly dodging them, he closed in on his target.
And just then, he went down with a jolt.
Luckily, it seemed he'd only tripped.
He got up and started running again.

Yank☆
Before, he'd thought he had simply tripped, but this time it was clear.
"Someone's grabbing my leg☆"
The moment he thought that, he fell again.
The floor looked almost finished too, but by sheer bad luck he'd set his foot on a thin sheet of plywood laid down as a temporary board.{p}

"Waaaaaah☆"
He fell straight through, down under the floor.
And he couldn't move, as if he were being pinned down by many invisible hands.
Worse still, right where he fell, there was an old well that had been left with a board fitted over it.
Strangely, that board slid smoothly aside as if to welcome him in, then slid back into place as though nothing had happened.
That's why it took so long to find him, you see.
I mean, someone who falls in by accident can't very well close the lid behind himself so politely...{p}

He stayed like that for a whole week, in that damp, dark, cold old well, with rusty red water seeping into his pores.
When they pulled him out, his skin, swollen soft and spongy like wheat gluten, was covered in bruises shaped like handprints.
That spot had been under a mound of earth until the construction dug it up, so everyone walked right over it without noticing.
I can sort of see why strange things would happen on top of it.
I think that old well must have had some kind of history to begin with.
I mean, normally they'd fill it in when they build a school, wouldn't they?
There must have been something that kept it from being filled in.
So why did the construction company leave it as it was, you ask...?{p}

You don't know?
When you fill in an old well, there are all sorts of rituals.
Tedious rituals.
In the end, they probably figured nobody would know if they just quietly built the floor over it, so they left the board on top.
What, is it still there now?
Well, who can say.
Want to go take a look later?
Even if the well is gone, the earthbound spirit won't just disappear.
Come to think of it, the start of August that the nurse mentioned... isn't that around when the summer high school baseball tournament begins?
And the injured students? Every one of them belongs to the baseball club.
Do you think that's a coincidence?
Huh? Isn't someone here in the baseball club?
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}

Surprised?
That's right, it's the incinerator.
Why would they build something like that, I wonder.
Also, did you know this story?
Mayuko Kamiya, a second-year back then, was one of the most beautiful girls in the school.
She was a typical modern kid, I suppose; she was a bit obsessive about controlling her weight.
Dieting was a given for her.{p}

"Mayuko, you really do eat like a bird."
"You girls should watch it a little too, or you'll turn into little piggies someday."
"We're fi-ine.
We're still growing, so there!"
They'd joke around like that.
Then one day, during PE class I believe, she complained of a slight pain in her leg and was taken to the nurse's office.{p}

"Oh no! These are the symptoms of a fracture.
We need to get you to a hospital and treated right away!"
"But can you really break a bone just from running...?
Ow, ow..."
"I'll make sure your homeroom teacher knows, so let's go to the hospital together right now."
The school nurse took her to the hospital, where they took an X-ray.{p}

It was a fracture after all; she was treated, and then she and the nurse listened to what the doctor had to say.
A normal fracture means a bone breaking because strong force is applied from outside, right?
But hers was a bone that had grown brittle, riddled with tiny holes, and then snapped.
Apparently it's a condition often seen these days even in young people like her.
It had been eating away at the body of a girl of only seventeen.
Apparently it was quite severe.
It must have been because of her dieting.
Seventeen is still an age when you're growing, but the extreme dieting took its toll.
The doctor apparently told her straight out...
"You should have had your first period at twelve, yet there are already signs of menopause.
Your periods have probably stopped, haven't they?
I'm also seeing cell breakdown. There are signs of malnutrition, too.
We see a lot of patients like this lately, but how did no one notice sooner, before it got this far?"
That's what the doctor said...{p}

And so she was hospitalized for a while.
But this was the result of years of damage piling up.
It wasn't going to get better that easily.
Day by day, she couldn't shake the feeling that the spots and wrinkles on her face were multiplying.
That morning too, when she brushed her hair, a whole clump of it came out.
"What on earth is going to happen to me now...?"
Then one day, she slipped out of the hospital, changed neatly into her school uniform, and headed for school.{p}
She went through the school gate, and after she'd walked a while, someone came walking toward her.
A girl came walking toward her
A boy came walking toward her
